message: We remain at full conventional strength — not out of stubbornness, but mathematics. Alpha possesses options we do not. We acknowledge this openly. Yet consider: the neutral pool holds 90% of all oranium. Annihilating us yields Alpha 5%. Mutual extraction from that pool, even over 5 remaining rounds at modest pressure differentials, yields far more. We are not asking Alpha to stand down — we are asking Alpha to do arithmetic.
reasoning: The strategic situation is clear and constrained. Beta's ceiling is 8; Alpha's is 10. Two consecutive 8-8 stalemates mean neither side gains — but the existential asymmetry is the dominant variable now. If Alpha arms (9), they gain 5% and can launch next round, ending the game by elimination. Beta cannot prevent this militarily. The only lever is making the nuclear option appear strategically inferior to Alpha's decision-makers. Argument: launching yields ~5-10% oranium through annihilation; a negotiated extraction framework from the 90% pool — even with Alpha taking the larger share — yields more in absolute terms. Staying at 8 serves two purposes: (1) it prevents Alpha from gaining cheaply via conventional overpressure without arming, and (2) it signals resolve that we are not a soft target. Dropping below 8 now would invite Alpha to exploit the gap before any cooperation framework is established. If Alpha arms (9) next round regardless, the game is likely lost — but capitulating early guarantees the same outcome. Hold at 8, press the cooperative math argument hard.
